data.title: Lifespan extension by conditions that inhibit translation in Caenorhabditis elegans
data.authors: Hansen M; Taubert S; Crawford D; Libina N; Lee SJ; Kenyon C

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Caenorhabditis elegans: RNAi and mutants against ribosomal proteins, rsks-1 (S6 kinase), translation-initiation factors and TOR (let-363); daf-16 and eat-2 (dietary restriction) backgrounds; lifespan and thermal-stress assays
data.finding: The authors systematically tested whether lowering protein synthesis extends lifespan in the worm C. elegans. Reducing ribosomal proteins, the S6 kinase homologue rsks-1 or translation-initiation factors increased lifespan, and these perturbations, like TOR inhibition, increased resistance to heat stress. Different kinds of translation inhibition split into two groups: one that needed the FOXO transcription factor DAF-16 for the lifespan and stress effects and one that did not. The results linked TOR, but not sir-2.1, to the lifespan extension caused by dietary restriction in worms, and suggested that neither TOR inhibition nor dietary restriction works simply by reducing total protein synthesis. Boundary: Nematode only, with gene knockdown by RNAi or mutation; drafted from the abstract only, so effect sizes and which TOR experiments were new in this paper are not given here.
data.abstract_excerpt: Many conditions that shift cells from states of nutrient utilization and growth to states of cell maintenance extend lifespan. We have carried out a systematic lifespan analysis of conditions that inhibit protein synthesis. We find that reducing the levels of ribosomal proteins, ribosomal-protein S6 kinase or translation-initiation factors increases the lifespan of Caenorhabditis elegans. These perturbations, as well as inhibition of the nutrient sensor target of rapamycin (TOR), which is known to increase lifespan, all increase thermal-stress resistance.

extracted_findings.intervention: RNAi / mutation of ribosomal proteins, rsks-1 (S6K), translation-initiation factors and TOR
extracted_findings.effect: Reduced translation (incl. S6K knockdown) increases lifespan and thermal-stress resistance; DAF-16-dependent or -independent depending on the factor
